A wounded dragon had nested near Karthspire. Forsworn worshippers occupied the surrounding ruins. Noctis needed support and believed the hunt would test Tsukihana's recovering body.
Katana arrived in time to say no before hearing the full proposal.
Tsukihana convinced her with the truth: if the marks returned, she needed witnesses capable of stopping her.
"If you collapse, he carries you," Katana said, pointing at Noctis.
"Agreed," Noctis replied.
Katana recognized the dragon pendant beneath his cloak and the scales caught in his armor. Noctis gave her a small warning shake of the head.
Tsukihana noticed the exchange but not its meaning.
They left before sunrise.
On the road, Tsukihana asked how many dragons Noctis had fought.
"Enough that counting stopped helping."
Ahead, Katana muttered, "She will understand when he starts shouting."
"What did you say?" Tsukihana asked.
"Nothing," both answered.

chapters.title: The Mark Answers
content: 4E 201 | Late Sun's Dusk | Eighty-Six Days Since Arrival
The wounded dragon nested inside ruined Reachmen towers blackened by fire.

Noctis took the cliff above. Katana and Tsukihana approached through a destroyed shrine. The plan was simple by his standards: draw the dragon's attention, break the ballista shaft lodged in its wing, keep it grounded, survive.
Noctis stepped from the cliff.
The dragon breathed fire at the falling man. He twisted through the flame, landed on its neck, and drove the creature's skull into the courtyard with the force of his strike.
Tsukihana and Katana moved.
Katana reached the wounded wing and shattered the ballista head with an enchanted knife. Tsukihana protected her from claws and tail, cutting only where necessary.
A horn sounded from the mountain.
Forsworn appeared on every ridge.
More than twenty ringed the ruins. Warriors shielded robed mages who linked their spells together. Flames spiraled above them, growing into a single fireball large enough to consume the courtyard.
Noctis was trapped beneath the dragon's assault. Katana searched for a path to the casters and found none.
"Run," she said.
There was nowhere to go.
Tsukihana inhaled.
The world sharpened. Eight sources. One spell. One center.
Cold breath left her lips.
The black marks surfaced beneath her right eye and spread down her arm. Crimson energy lifted her hair.
Katana seized her shoulder. "Promise me you can stop."
Tsukihana could not.
The fireball descended.
She stepped forward and thrust the katana into empty air.
A crimson line crossed the courtyard and pierced the spell's center. The burning mass compressed, split, and scattered across the sky like molten snow.
Tsukihana vanished.
She appeared within the Forsworn formation and shattered the first mage's staff before the man understood the spell had failed.
Noctis's Voice struck the ruins behind her.
"Joor Zah Frul!"
The dragon was hurled through a wall.
The truth of the stranger beside the fire rang through the mountain.
Noctis Arontis.
The Dragonborn.

chapters.title: Crimson Dance
content: 4E 201 | Late Sun's Dusk | Eighty-Six Days Since Arrival
Tsukihana remained conscious.
That changed everything.

She heard individual breaths within the Forsworn ring. Saw fingers tighten before spells formed. Felt weight shift through the ground. Her body no longer fought thought; movement and decision became the same thing.
It felt like dancing.
Six Forsworn attacked in succession.
Six fell in one flowing sequence.
Tsukihana looked at her marked hand. What are you?
More warriors surrounded her.
She extended her palm on instinct.
A crimson pulse burst outward and threw the entire circle into broken walls. With each attack she felt faster, stronger, more complete—and more afraid of how natural it felt.
Across the ruins, Noctis and the dragon unleashed Shouts that collided in a dome of force. Both were thrown apart.
Tsukihana vanished and caught Noctis before stone finished his momentum.
"I will press the offense," she said. "Take the opening."
Noctis nodded.
She appeared behind the dragon and released another point-blank pulse. The creature staggered. Her katana opened the leg, tail base, and damaged wing joint in rapid succession.
Noctis came from the blind side and drove his sword beneath the ribs. Katana planted enchanted knives in the healthy wing, forcing it closed.
Tsukihana struck beneath the jaw with crimson force.
Noctis leapt.
His blade entered the base of the dragon's throat.
Katana disabled the foreleg. Tsukihana widened the wound with two final cuts. Noctis twisted the sword.
The dragon shuddered and died.
For a breath the three stood amid blood, smoke, and broken Reach stone.
Katana looked from Noctis to Tsukihana. "That was terrible."
Noctis gave the faintest smile. "Efficient."
The corpse began to smoke from within.

chapters.title: What Remains After Fire
content: 4E 201 | Late Sun's Dusk | Eighty-Six Days Since Arrival
The dragon dissolved into bone.
Flesh became ash and golden-white energy poured into Noctis. The soul struck him like a storm, lifting dust and torn banners around the ruins. An ancient roar echoed where no living throat remained.
Tsukihana's power reacted. The marks tightened across her skin.
She closed her eyes and breathed out.
"Enough."
The aura folded inward. The black lines vanished. She dropped to one knee, shaking but conscious.
Katana checked her pupils, breathing, and memory in rapid succession.
Noctis searched the dead mages and found ritual marks carved into their flesh. The Forsworn had not intended to worship the dragon forever. They meant to bind it with old occult magic.
"Nothing good comes from people who believe a dragon is a tool," he said.
Tsukihana stood and sheathed her sword in one clean motion.
She looked at the dead.
"Since I came to this land, there has been one fight after another. Blood, curses, graves, war. Is that all Skyrim is?"
Noctis studied the mountain road.

"Violence is loud," he said. "A town surviving winter never becomes a song. A healer staying beside a sick child is not carved into a palace wall. Burn a village, kill a king, wake something buried—everyone remembers."
Tsukihana thought of Zaria's potions, Runil's blessing, Inigo's jokes, Katana sleeping beside her bed.
"Skyrim is cruel," Noctis continued. "But that is not all it is. Walk long enough."
A dying Forsworn mage coughed beneath a fallen beam.
"The wyrm was not the offering," he whispered.
His eyes fixed on Tsukihana.
"The red moon has opened. Seven masks. Seven graves. The city beneath stone."
He died after naming the sword and what slept inside her.
Noctis revealed that the masked man he followed had taken a trail deeper into the mountains.
Exhaustion argued against pursuit.
The Calamities being ahead of them argued louder.
They followed.

chapters.title: The Calamity of Blood
content: 4E 201 | Late Sun's Dusk | Eighty-Six Days Since Arrival
The mountain trail opened into an abandoned camp covered in maps, ritual diagrams, and scrolls.
The Forsworn had received the dragon-binding spell from a stranger wearing a white porcelain mask veined with crimson. Hidden inside the spell was a cipher none of them understood.
Noctis identified binding points. Katana found notes stating that the visible ritual was simplified and that the governing structure had been concealed inside the chant.
Tsukihana packed the pages. "We need a scholar of magic."
"Calcelmo," Katana said. "He likes old scripts and being correct."
They continued toward a house and mine built against the cliff.
The Forsworn who occupied it were already dead.
Bodies lay twisted beyond anatomy. Blood formed deliberate lines across the dirt. Some corpses had been drained into leather and bone. Others were pinned to walls by hardened crimson spears.
Noctis stopped. "Prepare yourselves."
A shockwave burst from the mine.
They held their ground.

A tall figure stepped from the darkness, silver hair flowing over black and crimson clothing. A porcelain mask concealed his face. Blood orbited his bare hands in delicate ribbons, blades, hooks, and flowering constructs.
He held a journal and wrote with a stylus formed from blood.
Then he bowed.
"Eryx," he said. "The Calamity of Blood."
His masked attention settled on Tsukihana. "Mei had so much to say about you."
Tsukihana drew. "What do you want?"
Eryx waved elegantly. "Do not worry. I am not after you today. I was recording the results of my experiments before I sensed a foul presence."
He turned toward Noctis.
"A Dovahkiin wearing stolen souls like perfume. Offensive."
Noctis placed a hand on his sword. "You wear corpses as tools."
"A necessary distinction."
Eryx explained that blood carried memory, fear, lineage, and potential. The dead Forsworn had been material: altered by ritual magic, then tested to see how their blood responded to pressure.
"You murdered them for notes," Tsukihana said.
"No. I murdered them for knowledge. Notes merely prevent knowledge from becoming wasteful."
Blood rose from every corpse.
The bodies stood on broken limbs.
Eryx closed his journal.

chapters.title: Fellow Traitor
content: 4E 201 | Late Sun's Dusk | Eighty-Six Days Since Arrival
Eryx looked at Noctis one final time.
"Until we meet again, fellow traitor."
His body dissolved into a cloud of blood before Tsukihana's strike reached him.
The mist vanished into the ground.
The controlled corpses attacked.
Cutting them apart did nothing. Severed torsos crawled. Detached hands retained weapons through blood threads. Wounds closed beneath red membranes as Eryx's command repaired the dead.
Tsukihana saw the system before the others did. Every crimson thread led toward a symbol painted across the mine entrance.
Katana threw enchanted knives. Blood tendrils intercepted and absorbed the blasts.
The marionettes closed from all sides.
The black marks surfaced across Tsukihana's hand.
She felt the blood command: one network, multiple bodies, a single source.
Tsukihana extended her hand and clenched it.
Every corpse froze.
Eryx's magic fought her grip. Her arm shook as black lines spread toward her elbow.
"I cannot hold them," she said.
Noctis faced the mine entrance.
"You do not need long."
His Shout shattered the blood symbol and collapsed the outer tunnel.
The threads snapped.
Every corpse fell.
Afterward Tsukihana asked why Eryx had called Noctis a traitor.
"Was he lying?"
"No," Noctis said.
"A traitor to whom?" Katana asked.
"People you do not want finding you."
He refused more, calling it his responsibility until disclosure would not place additional enemies behind them.
They found a map on one corpse: seven crimson lines converging beneath Markarth around a single ciphered word.
Awakening.
Tsukihana accepted Noctis's silence only for the moment.
Far away, Eryx wrote in his journal:
The Dragonborn reacts to accusation. The Moon vessel can interrupt external blood commands. Consciousness remains intact during partial awakening. Both traitors are more complete than expected.

chapters.title: Threads Beneath Markarth
content: 4E 201 | Late Sun's Dusk | Ninety Days Since Arrival
Noctis left Markarth after another dragon sighting.
A few days later, Tsukihana and Katana carried the cipher into Understone Keep. Turning left from the main hall brought them into an excavation chamber dominated by a newly revealed Dwarven entrance.
Calcelmo stood among maps and tools, attempting to work while Remiel asked questions faster than he could resent them.
"Did the ring rotate before the earthquake?"
"Yes."
"Did you apply external magicka?"
"No."
"Why not?"
"Because I enjoy having a ceiling."
Remiel saw Tsukihana and waved. "You're alive!"
Calcelmo turned at the mention of two destroyed Colossi and looked as if someone had burned a library.

Beside the maps stood a Redguard woman in layered black and deep green mage attire threaded with gold. Thick braids and curls framed amber eyes that studied Tsukihana and Katana with immediate, amused intelligence.
Katana asked who she was.
The woman stepped forward with a smirk and extended one hand.
"Raya. Dear friend of Remiel, scholar, mage, occasional voice of reason, and apparently sarcastic at times. Who are you two?"
"Tsukihana Kurogane."
"Black iron," Raya translated. "A name meant for steel."
"Katana."
Raya waited for more and received none.
Tsukihana placed the ritual pages before Calcelmo. He identified a second spell hidden within the first. Raya's Threadborn vision revealed golden paths of magic between the runes.
"The cipher is collecting residual energy," she said. "Fear, blood, magicka, the dragon's resistance, the failed binding."
The visible ritual had never been designed to control the dragon.
It had been bait for whatever answered.
The newly exposed Dwarven door began to glow.
Circular rings rotated. At the center appeared the symbol of the Seven Calamities.
The doors opened.
Cold air poured from the darkness.
Somewhere below, something drew a blade.

chapters.title: The Ruin That Should Not Exist
content: 4E 201 | Late Sun's Dusk | Ninety Days Since Arrival
Calcelmo forbade entry.
Remiel began packing equipment.
The newly revealed ruin had no place in Markarth's archives. Its metal composition differed from known Dwemer structures. The Calamities' symbol had been cut too cleanly to be ancient.
Raya examined the threshold with Threadborn vision. Seven dark magical paths extended inward. One carried frost. Another pulsed like blood.
Mei and Eryx had been there.
Tsukihana, Katana, Raya, and Remiel entered while Calcelmo and Aicantar remained outside to study the door and operate it if necessary.
The ruin smelled of rain despite lying beneath the mountain.

Bronze conduits ran through dark stone like veins. The first corpse they found was a Forsworn woman with blackened eyes and no wounds. A sharpened key fragment rested in her hand, cut with seven grooves.
When Raya sealed the fragment inside a specimen case, the dead woman inhaled once and died again.
"Something inside the key maintained an imitation," Raya said.
"Blood magic?" Tsukihana asked.
"No. Memory."
A blade scraped along stone in the right-hand passage.
Raya sent a sphere of fire ahead.
Rows of alcoves appeared. Desiccated bodies stood within bronze frames: Nords, Imperials, Reachmen, mages, warriors, some ancient and some recent.
At the final alcove stood a corpse in Blades armor holding a katana.
The old weapon across Tsukihana's back grew heavy.
The corpse raised its head.
"Successor identified," said a voice from the bronze frame behind it. "Key fragment detected. Transfer required."
It attacked.
The dead Blade's swordsmanship was disciplined, swift, and close enough to Akaviri forms that Tsukihana recognized the philosophy. Katana joined, yet the corpse held both blades.
Bronze channels flared.
Every preserved body opened its eyes.
Above them, the entrance began to close. Calcelmo's shout vanished beneath grinding metal.
The dead Blade returned its katana to the sheath and lowered into a quick-draw stance.
"Prove continuity."
Tsukihana mirrored him.
Her thumb pressed against the guard.
Two inheritors faced one another across centuries: one alive, one preserved because the ruin refused to release the past.
The bronze channels flashed crimson.
Both swords left their sheaths.
And the ruin chose its successor.

END OF THE CURRENT MANUSCRIPT
